analysis.title: BofA on USA: Weekly spending update through Nov 14
key_insights: Total card spending per household rose 5.2% y/y in the week ending Nov 14, per BAC aggregated credit and debit card data, up from 5.1% on Nov 7.
Versus the prior week, y/y entertainment spending growth rose the most (-3.6% on Nov 7 to 13.5% on Nov 14). Gas spending growth slowed the most (20.2% to 16.5%).
Lower-income spending growth has consistently outpaced higher-income spending growth over the past several weeks (total card ex gas, per household).
Total card ex gas spending was up 4.6% y/y in the week ending Nov 14, versus 4.4% on Nov 7.
Airline spending growth accelerated to 17.5% y/y on Nov 14 from 4.1% on Nov 7. Transit rose to 8.2% from 4.2%.
Retail ex-autos spending growth was 3.8% y/y on Nov 14, versus 4.1% on Nov 7. Online retail grew 5.8% and brick-and-mortar retail 2.7%.
Furniture (-6.9%), department stores (-1.9%) and grocery (+0.5%) remained the weakest categories on Nov 14. General merchandise slowed to 6.1% from 8.4% on Nov 7.
Ahead of the holiday season, total card spending is running well ahead of last year's levels. Spending on holiday items is up 5.5% relative to the same period 52 weeks ago.

macro_indicators.indicator: Retail ex-autos card spending per household (y/y, 7-day MA)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Retail spending growth is slightly below its 4.1% reading on Nov 7.

macro_indicators.indicator: Holiday items card spending per household (y/y)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Holiday-category spending is running above last year's pace.

risk_factors: BAC card data have selection bias in income levels and geographies, exclude cash, checks and ACH payments, and are not comprehensive, so they should be read alongside other economic indicators.
